newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed amid cross deals.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed amid cross deals.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in markets dominated by cross deals and demand for blue chip shares, traders said.

Bogota's IBB index ended its six-day run of gains and drifted down 0.29 percent to 841.22 in 1.6 billion peso volume. Medellin's IBOMED general price index edged up 0.1 percent to 13,331.72 in volume of 1.2 billion pesos.

"There were a lot of cross deals and demand for easy-to-sell shares from people who are looking for year-end tax breaks. The supermarket chains, on the other hand, fell because there was no real demand there," a Bogota broker said.

The Bogota index was dragged down by a 4.49 percent dip in supermarket chain Cadenalco, down to 850 on 106.7 million pesos traded, and a 1.83 percent drop in Carulla supermarkets, down to 5,350 in volume of 1.95 million pesos.

"There's been quite a lot of speculation in the supermarket chains of late, particularly by foreign funds. And today there wasn't enough demand to soak up the abundant supply put up by small investors," the broker added.
Demand for Banco de Bogota shares remained firm. It ended 0.41 percent up at 6,025 amid trade of 228.9 million pesos. Brewing giant Bavaria also climbed 0.47 percent to 4,035.

Another of the major trades on the Bogota exchange was a 424 million peso cross deal in cement manufacturer Cementos Argos, part of the Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, whose shares remained unchanged at 5,300 each.

Activity in the Medellin exchange centered on deals in insurance company Suramericana de Seguros, unchanged at 18,500 in trade of 862 million pesos, and in cigarrette manufacturer Coltabaco, unchanged at 3,000. Machinery and industrial equipment manufacturer Distral SA surged 6.6 percent to 31.67, on the back of continued speculation that a foreign company may enter into a partnership with Distral.
"There are rumors that a German or a U.S. company want to take control of the company," a Medelln broker said.

Meanwhile, mining concern Mineros de Antioqua plunged 18.9 percent to 165 in volume of 4.78 million pesos. Brokers blamed the drop on investor fears about the law and order situation in Colombia's northwest where the company operates.
